 Flood Watch issued across Hawaiian Islands as remnants of Olana soak the Aloha State with intense downpours
 The interaction between the storms and Hawaii's tall mountains will raise the risk of flash flooding, with 5 to 8 inches of rain possible from Oahu to the Big Island.

 02:21 Hawaii under Flood Watch as remnants of Olana soak the state with intense downpours 
 A Flood Watch is in effect through Wednesday night across the entire state of Hawaii as the remnants of Olana soak the state with heavy downpours. The interaction between the storms and Hawaii's tall mountains will raise the risk of flash flooding, with 5 to 8 inches of rain possible from Oahu to the Big Island. Rain is expected to linger through Friday.
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 A Flood Watch is in effect through Wednesday night across the entire state of Hawaii as the remnants of Olana soak the state.
 Olana has weakened into a remnant low, after briefly becoming a topical storm Sunday.
 While Olana became post-tropical before reaching Hawaii, it's been an active hurricane season for a state which rarely sees tropical activity.

 WHAT IS AN INVEST DURING HURRICANE SEASON? 
 Tropical moisture will interact directly with Hawaii's mountainous terrain, as air is forced up tall mountain slopes, it cools, producing heavy rain, potentially triggering mudslides .
 Vehicles make their way through a flooded intersection in front of the Hawaii Convention Center in Honolulu, Hawaii, on August 16, 2026. Hurricane Lala was pulling away from Hawaii's Big Island early Sunday, as heavy rain and strong winds struck the US Pacific state and officials warned of potentially dangerous flooding. The heavy rain and flood risk will then spread westward across the island chain on Sunday, according to the NHC.

 Maui County officials warned residents and tourists to be ready for intense downpours.
 WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A TROPICAL DEPRESSION, TROPICAL STORM AND HURRICANE? 
 Rain is expected to linger through Friday.
 Wind gusts are expected to increase as the system becomes more organized.
 The heaviest rain will sweep from the south and west-facing slopes of the islands; this will create varying effects for different landscapes, as the direction of the rain will play a vital role in determining where the worst flooding will be.
 KA'A'AWA, HI - MARCH 3:  A fire fighter squeegies water away from a flooded home on March 3, 2006 in the town of Ka'aa'wa on the Windward side of Oahu, Hawaii.  Fire fighers and police from all over Oahu worked overtime to help residents on the WIndward side clean up after the flooding in the area. Days of heavy rains on Oahu have flooded roads, caused several landslides and closed schools. Many homes in the area have suffered minor flooding. Fire fighers and police from all over Oahu worked overtime to help residents on the WIndward side clean up after the flooding in the area.  More rain is expected next week.  The Hawaiian Governor has declared a state of emergency.  The Hawaii National Guard is on alert to evacuate people who are in areas prone to flooding.

 "The direction the rain is moving from does matter," the FOX Forecast Center said. "Rain moving in from the southwest is much different than west-moving tropical systems that move from the East Pacific."
 This wave of storms over the next few days is just the beginning, as another storm system could develop west of Hawaii for Halloween weekend, bringing even more rain to the Aloha State.

 (FOX Weather) 
 While Olana became post-tropical before reaching Hawaii, it's been an active hurricane season for a state which rarely sees tropical activity. Hawaii saw a direct hit from major Hurricane Lowell in early September, in addition to close passes from Lala, Moke and Nolo.
